correctness.rationale: Theorem is proved by exact pseudohyperbolic slice integration for V and the coordinate second moment, Bergman kernel covariance under a diagonal Möbius automorphism, rotation/swap symmetry which makes the sum and difference coordinate Gram matrix diagonal, and the exact I_s=V coefficient identity. The second Gram norm equals 4I_u−V. All quantifiers include every rho in (0,1), every a in the disk, and both metric directions. A covariance derivative proves strict monotonicity, and exact logarithmic moment formulae yield rigorously the sharp 10/3 and 4 endpoint coefficients. Executable mpmath/Sympy calculations check formulas; finite experiments do not substitute for the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The exact normal-vs-tangential Bergman metric deformation is a natural quantitative invariant of the intrinsic geometry of Pick interpolation domains. Strict monotonicity captures the full node-separation range; the sharp reciprocal-square and logarithmic phase-boundary behaviors quantify markedly different singular limits. It meaningfully strengthens qualitative knowledge of interpolation domains and automorphisms, rather than tabulating an unmotivated special case. Its precise scope is a full natural two-node family restricted to its diagonal, not a claim of general multipoint classification.
